S No directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  CRLA No. 389 of 2015  Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Ms. Sonia Chawla, learned counsel for the applicant/appellant.
2. Mr. J.S. Virk, learned D.A.G. alongwith Mr. R.K. Joshi, learned Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.

3. Appellant is convicted for offence punishable under Sections 376(2), 363, 365 and 366 IPC r/w Section 6 of the POCSO Act and was mainly awarded life imprisonment with fine of Rs.50,000/.
Presently, he is lodged in Central Jail, Sitarganj.
4.
Appellant has sought short term bail application on the ground of illness of his father.
It is contended that there is no other male member in the family to take care of his father, who has suffered paralytic attack and referred to higher center.
5. Learned State Counsel was asked to get instructions.

Today, on instructions, he submits that the medical records annexed with the short-term bail application are genuine, and he confirmed the fact that the appellant's father is suffering from paralysis.

6. Having regard to the fact that the appellant is in jail continuously ever since 12.03.2015 and was never granted short- term bail earlier, we are inclined to grant short term bail to the appellant for a period of three weeks from the date of his release, on his executing personal bond with two reliable sureties, each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Magistrate concerned.
7. Three weeks shall be counted from the date of his actual release.
However, after expiry of the period of short-term bail granted by this Court, the appellant shall surrender before the Authority concerned.
